transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-30 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Ruth (Redwood SE), Maya (Apex CTO), Jordan (Eng Lead), Priya (Security), Ethan (ML)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, really appreciate it. Quick intros - I'm Samir Patel, AE at Redwood, and Ruth is our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Maya: Hi all, Maya here, CTO at Apex Ventures. We're evaluating for a customer-facing assistant and some internal summarization, trying to understand time-to-first-token and cost.
[00:18] Jordan: Jordan, engineering lead. Interested in how quickly we can get a test up and running and what the dev experience looks like.
[00:24] Priya: Priya from security. We'll be focused on data residency, audit logs, KMS.
[00:29] Ruth: Great, thanks. We'll run through quickstart, free credits, and then deeper on hosting options — hosted API for PLG, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem).
[00:41] Samir: High-level — Redwood offers a hosted API you can self-serve into, we give new accounts free credits to experiment, and our quickstart typically gets folks to first-token within minutes.
[00:51] Ethan: When you say minutes, like how many steps, is there a CLI or SDK?
[00:56] Ruth: We have SDKs (Python/Node), plus a curl example. Typical flow: sign up, verify email, create API key, run curl or pip install redwood, then a single sample call. In my experience it's ~5-10 mins if you have an account already.
[01:10] Jordan: Any friction with SSO or corporate networks? We use Okta and have strict egress.
[01:15] Samir: For quickstart you can use a personal API key, Okta SSO is available for org onboarding — that comes with SCIM and SAML options. For corporate egress you can also use VPC peering if we move to Dedicated or Private later.
[01:30] Maya: For the quick POC we want hosted to reduce setup time. But security will likely push for Dedicated or Private if we ship to customers.
[01:38] Priya: Yes, main concerns: SOC 2, audit logs, encryption at rest and in transit, customer KMS support. Also data retention policies.
[01:45] Ruth: We are SOC 2 compliant, have customer audit logs, and the Private option supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. Hosted has encryption and RBAC, Dedicated gives an extra isolation layer with reserved GPU pools. We'll share the security pack.
[01:59] Jordan: Cool. On the model side — do you host open models or proprietary ones? Latency expectations?
[02:05] Ruth: We host a curated catalog of open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. For latency, depends on model and token length; for typical chat traffic a small to medium model on hosted will be ~200-400ms p95, Dedicated can be tuned for tighter SLOs. We also do batching and KV cache to optimize cost.
[02:23] Ethan: If we want to run benchmarks, what's the recommended approach? We want to compare cost/latency against an in-house baseline.
[02:28] Ruth: We'll give you a bench checklist — include your prompt set, expected concurrency, and typical sequence lengths. For quickstart you can run a small load test from your account; for more controlled benchmarks we can run a redwood-managed test on Dedicated with a canary config.
[02:40] Samir: I'll include sample curl/SDK snippets and an estimate for free credits — usually enough for a few thousand requests depending on model.
[02:49] Maya: On pricing — are the hosted tiers pay-as-you-go? How does Dedicated commit work?
[02:54] Samir: Hosted is usage-based per-token for generation and per-unit for embeddings. Dedicated is reserved capacity — monthly or annual commits, gives predictable throughput and a discount vs on-demand. We'll send the price sheet.
[03:07] Jordan: Any rate limiting or quotas for the free trial?
[03:10] Ruth: Yes, free accounts have soft rate limits to protect the platform; we can raise them during a POC if needed.
[03:16] Priya: For audit purposes we need logs of who called what and ability to rotate keys. Does Redwood store user prompts by default?
[03:24] Samir: For hosted, we have opt-in data retention for logging; by default short-term logs are kept for debugging and you can opt out. For Dedicated/Private we support no-logging modes and customer-managed storage. Key rotation is supported via API and your KMS integration for Private.
[03:40] Maya: How about time-to-first-token in the SDK? Does the SDK download model artifacts or is it just API wrappers?
[03:47] Ruth: SDK is a lightweight wrapper — no model downloads. Time-to-first-token is mainly dependent on network and model choice. For local/private deployments there may be additional setup time.
[03:56] Jordan: Any gotchas with tokenization differences or pricing surprises? We deal with large context windows and long docs.
[04:02] Ruth: We surface token counts in the console and have tooling to estimate cost given sequence lengths. Long-context models are billed accordingly; quantization profiles for Dedicated can reduce cost. We'll recommend a profile based on your evals.
[04:16] Ethan: We plan to test embeddings for retrieval-augmented generation too. Do you provide embedding endpoints and batch embeddings?
[04:22] Ruth: Yes, embeddings endpoint, and batching is supported. Also caching suggestions in Redwood Optimize to reduce duplicate compute.
[04:30] Maya: Ok, practical next steps from our side: get quickstart, confirm pilot dataset, and security team will review docs.
[04:36] Samir: Agreed — for the quickstart you'll get an invite link to create an account with free credits, Ruth will drop the bench checklist and curl/SDK snippets, and I'll send pricing and Dedicated/Private one-pager.
[04:47] Priya: We'll need the SOC 2 report and KMS integration doc. Also questions about on-prem package for air-gapped deployment.
[04:54] Ruth: We'll attach the security pack that includes SOC 2, ISO snippets, and our Private on-prem checklist. On-prem is possible but will need planning, timelines, and support level.
[05:06] Jordan: If we want to get a basic chat working, what's the minimal prompt flow and expected latency?
[05:11] Ruth: Minimal flow: single API call to /v1/generate or chat endpoint with model selection. For a mid-size open model you can expect 200-500ms first token in hosted. If you need streaming we support that too.
[05:23] Samir: I'll summarize in an email and include links: quickstart repo, sample curl, SDK, pricing, and security pack.
[05:29] Maya: Perfect. When can we schedule a technical POC? Week of Jan 9 sounds good.
[05:34] Samir: I'll propose slots after I send the email.
[05:37] Ruth: Any other technical blockers?
[05:39] Ethan: Just making sure we can reproduce locally and run a small load test, should be fine.
[05:44] Priya: I'll review security docs and come back with a short list of requirements.
[05:48] Samir: Great, thanks everyone.
[05:50] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.

Meeting recap: PLG quickstart for hosted API is the immediate path. Customer wants free credits and a fast time-to-first-token to validate use cases (chat + embeddings). Long-term considerations: Dedicated for predictable throughput and Private for on-prem/KMS/audit needs. Action items and next steps captured.

References shared: "Quickstart repo link (shared by Ruth)", "Security pack (SOC2 + KMS details) - will be attached", "Pricing sheet (Samir)"

Notes on transcript: minor transcription errors present (product names sometimes misheard), speakers occasionally overlap, natural speech patterns preserved.
